items.title: Billy McBride and Mary McBride ("Mack and Mack") Interview, 1959-07-01
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I believe he's dead. Somebody told me he's, uh, Cootie Williams' teacher, I believe, too. Yeah. Did you know Cootie Williams, who played with Ellington? Sure. I know him.

ctx.x: Ha, ha, ha. But, uh, do you remember that Excelsior Band? Yeah. Yeah. I remember them for the reason that, uh, uh, in Mobile, being born, they, you know, they, they lived, uh, uh, what they called the Creoles in Mobile. They were Creoles, you know. Yeah. Yeah. And, and... Yes, he's very light. Yeah, yeah. See, and they didn't really, uh, mix too much with the rest of the colored people. And so, that's why I remember them so well. But I think this fellow, one of the musicians, who was named Willie, Pope or…

I believe he's dead. Somebody told me he was, uh, Cootie Williams' teacher, I believe, too. Yeah. Did you know Cootie Williams, who played with Ellington? Sure. I know him. There's another old man whom I didn't get to meet, who still is there. I'll meet him my next trip. They called him Chicken. Some people said they could only remember his name. No. It was Chicken. Do you remember that name?
No. Well, there was a fellow called Charlie Chicken Jones, but I think he's dead.
